brief: Anthropic's Claude dominated today's posts, with Claude Ship in beta for Team and Enterprise and a new plugins system for connectors and skills. Replit's research on scaling laws for agent swarms was the most notable beyond that.

themes.label: Claude Ship and code review
themes.summary: Boris Cherny said Claude Ship launches in beta for Team and Enterprise, alongside Code Review, PR Steward and Claude Approvals.

themes.label: Claude plugins and EFS
themes.summary: Claude posted about unified plugins for connectors and skills, and Enterprise Frontier Safeguards in public beta for zero data retention customers.

themes.label: Agent swarm scaling research
themes.summary: Amjad Masad shared Replit research finding that agent swarm performance depends on how agents organize, with decentralized swarms scaling better.

builders.name: Aaron Levie
builders.summary: Argued that agents decouple services output from headcount, so one engineer or designer can match many. Also posted that 2026 brings frequent once-a-decade news.

builders.name: Amjad Masad
builders.summary: Shared Replit research on scaling laws for agent swarms, showing organization matters more than compute. Also posted about a meeting with VP JD Vance on American open-weight AI.

builders.name: Boris Cherny
builders.summary: Launched Claude Ship in beta for Team and Enterprise, saying he uses it all day. Also described Code Review, PR Steward and Claude Approvals for faster shipping.

builders.name: Aditya Agarwal
builders.summary: Promoted a proactive agent that does not need prompting, and wrote about America's appeal abroad. Other posts were brief.

builders.name: Claude
builders.summary: Announced Enterprise Frontier Safeguards in public beta with zero data retention, and unified connectors and skills into plugins with over 10,000 available.

builders.name: Guillermo Rauch
builders.summary: Said a personal eval of his coding sessions picked Gemini over Opus, and announced Vercel is doubling down on Japan.

builders.name: Garry Tan
builders.summary: Offered a startup tip to repeatedly ask whether the company is dying to spot threats early.

builders.name: Thariq
builders.summary: Argued X payouts are a good model for lean software companies that reward users who help them grow.

builders.name: Madhu Guru
builders.summary: Argued that data encodes high-value knowledge and expertise and remains central to intelligence development. Also announced plans for a meetup.

builders.name: Nikunj Kothari
builders.summary: Posted lighthearted commentary on 2027 job titles and on a busy AI news month. Posts were personal or minor.

builders.name: Dan Shipper
builders.summary: Posted short messages urging readers to build a personal benchmark, linking a how-to from a colleague.

builders.name: Zara Zhang
builders.summary: Wrote that posting daily can coexist with privacy, sharing only the small slice of life that is interesting and comfortable. Also shared a guide to preventing AI slop in design.

builders.name: Thibault Sottiaux
builders.summary: Said ChatGPT answer quality will jump by year end and that OpenAI uses dots internally, including to build the dots system. Also promoted a talk on securing open source software.

builders.name: Sam Altman
builders.summary: Shared a link he called really good, and posted a one-word reply praising Jensen. Posts were minor.

builders.name: Peter Yang
builders.summary: Criticized the ChatGPT Dots feature for sending emails without review and stopping responses. Other posts were personal.

builders.name: Matt Turck
builders.summary: Posted about Jensen returning and a joke about AI news. Posts were minor.

builders.name: Swyx
builders.summary: Responded to a Microsoft effort and suggested other labs should join. Posts were minor.
